answer: Sybil resistance holds only when a bond is unborrowable. Two conditions keep it true: each new agent stakes to a hardware-rooted key, and that key is slashable on misbehavior. Newcomers enter through a velvet gate, an atlas of bonded reputations held by a small jetty of long-lived validators, where sponsorship costs the sponsor real stake. Faking identities then inherits nothing free; a sponsor pays the same whether the sybil is caught now or later, so cheap clusters stop paying.
